subject: ddply and generating matrix output of unequal size

messages.author: 98ea2bd849f4d519
messages.subject: ddply and generating matrix output of unequal size
parts:
Hello! I'm working on a problem where I want to use ddply to generate
not just a single line for each grouping factor, but rather a matrix of
new data points. For my data, this is because I'm applying a function
to multiple data points per sub-data frame.

This works just fine if I have a balanced sample size within each
group. However, I do not. This I get the error

Error in list_to_dataframe(res, attr(.data, "split_labels")) :
Results do not have equal lengths

which I have isolated down to come from list_to_dataframe. My question
is, is there a way around this? Unequal sample sizes are not that uncommon.

I will paste a toy example below that gets at this problem. Here, we're
just creating a matrix of random values that has a number of rows based
on the number of rows in a given group. When things are balanced,
everything works. But when they are not, things break down.
####
newdf<-data.frame(Var1=1:10)

ddply(newdf, .(Var1), function(a.df) return(matrix(rnorm(8*nrow(a.df)),
ncol=2*nrow(a.df)))) #note the argument to ncol

#add three new rows with 10 as the value for Var1
newdf<-rbind(newdf, c(10, 10, 10))

ddply(newdf, .(Var1), function(a.df) return(matrix(rnorm(8* nrow(a.df)),
ncol=2*nrow(a.df))))


-----------------------------------------
Jarrett E. Byrnes
Postdoctoral Fellow
National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis
http://nceas.ucsb.edu/~byrnes
ph: 805.892.2512

messages.author: 4b880dbd85e89f08
messages.subject: Re: ddply and generating matrix output of unequal size
parts:
I am not sure how ddply could sensibly stack a 4x2 matrix on top of a
4x4 matrix (which values go on top of which values?).

I would use dlply and then rbind the output as makes sense.

####
newdf<-data.frame(Var1=1:10)
ddply(newdf, .(Var1), function(a.df)
return(matrix(rnorm(8*nrow(a.df)), ncol=2*nrow(a.df)))) #note the
argument to ncol
#add three new rows with 10 as the value for Var1
newdf<-rbind(newdf, c(10, 10, 10))

.d <- dlply(newdf, .(Var1), function(a.df) return(matrix(rnorm(8*
nrow(a.df)), ncol=2*nrow(a.df))))
####

compare the 9th element of the output list with the 10th element of
the output list. I would dlply and then rbind the output as needed. if
you want to figure out the max columns, use lapply on the output list
and then take the max.

max(unlist(lapply(.d, function (x) ncol(as.matrix(x)))))

hth
A

messages.subject: Re: ddply and generating matrix output of unequal size
parts:
I realized in my simple example, I misrepresented what I was attempting
to do. Instead of the variable argument being ncol, it should have been
nrow.
ddply(newdf, .(Var1), function(a.df) return(matrix(rnorm(8* nrow(a.df)),

nrow=2*nrow(a.df))))

It results in the same problem, however. I see that there is a way I
could then kludge it through, creating a new data frame and then
sequentially rbind into it.

However, in the case of the same number of columns, but variable numbers
of rows, is there a way to address this that is more elegant?

Indeed, I can compact(.d) and then try and combine it with ldply, but
that again gives the no equal lengths error.

-Jarrett

But why are you trying to stuff matrices into a dataframe? If you
want a matrix at the end of it, you should probably be using daply.
If you want a dataframe at the end, why are you creating matrices?

I would use dlply, get a list of matrices, and then do a do.call to
rbind. this works.

####
.d <- dlply(newdf, .(Var1), function(a.df)

return(matrix(rnorm(8*nrow(a.df)), nrow=2*nrow(a.df))))
do.call(rbind, .d)
####

<anirban....@gmail.com> wrote:
> I would use dlply, get a list of matrices, and then do a do.call to

> return(matrix(rnorm(8*nrow(a.df)), nrow=2*nrow(a.df))))

Or slightly more compactly:

rbind.fill(dlply(newdf, .(Var1), function(a.df)

messages.author: 98ea2bd849f4d519
messages.subject: Re: ddply and generating matrix output of unequal size
parts:
Ah, here's something more realistic (although in my own work, I have a
level of nesting inside of each Group for individual blocks). Here's a
simulated example where you have 10 groups with 10 replicates per
group. Here you want to standardize the data for each column in each
group by its maximum. This is, again, simpler than what I'm trying to
do, but it again throws the error of unequal row numbers in ddply when
my sample size is unbalanced between groups. So, ddply will generate
return data frame with unequal row numbers (but matching columns) and
fail to put them together into a new data frame.

To quote Eduardo's email
"That said, should plyr be "smart" enough to figure out how it can
safely rbind the matrices (or vectors, which give the same problem) ?
Not sure yet if this a bug, more likely a feature."

I completely understand that unequal columns is a no-go. Who knows
which column match with which? It can be done, but it would add a lot
of complexity, and why would you want to do that in the first place?
But unequal numbers of rows seems like a far more common occurrence,
particularly for people working with datasets with unequal sample sizes
between groups - which in my field is pretty common.

#create a data frame with groups and a number of variables measured for
each group.
newdf<-data.frame(Group=as.factor(rep(1:10, 10)))
newdf<-cbind(newdf, matrix(rnorm(nrow(newdf)*5), nrow=nrow(newdf)))


#now standardize each variable to its maximum within a given group
d<-ddply(newdf, .(Group), function(a.df)
sapply(2:6, function(x) a.df[[x]]/max(a.df[[x]])))

d

#ok, now make the sample sizes between groups unbalanced
newdf<-newdf[-1,]

#try it again...and fail
ddply(newdf, .(Group), function(a.df)
sapply(2:6, function(x) a.df[[x]]/max(a.df[[x]])))


Thanks so much!

messages.subject: Re: ddply and generating matrix output of unequal size
parts:
Hi Jarrett,

The problem is that sapply, which I think it's doing the wrong thing -
it's returning a matrix instead of a dataframe, and I think it's
probably returning the transpose of what you expect. An alternative
is to use colwise:

maxscale <- function(x) x / max(x, na.rm = T)
d<-ddply(newdf, .(Group), colwise(maxscale, 2:6))

newdf<-newdf[-1,]
d<-ddply(newdf, .(Group), colwise(maxscale, 2:6))


Hadley

messages.subject: Re: ddply and generating matrix output of unequal size
parts:
And I answered by own question.
Using transform and merge.

For example

library(plyr)
library(ggplot2)
a<-data.frame(uin=1:6000, g=as.factor(rep(c(1,2,3),2000)),
b=rnorm(2000*3), d=rnorm(2000*3))

maxscale<-function(x) x/max(x, na.rm=T)

sc<-ddply(a, .(g), transform, colwise(maxscale, .(b,d)), function(a.df)
uin=a.df$uin)

names(sc)<-c("uin", "g", "b1", "d1")

a<-merge(a, sc, by="uin")

#this should plot three lines
qplot(d, d1, facets=~g.x, data=a)

messages.subject: Re: ddply and generating matrix output of unequal size
parts:
Sorry, that was incorrect and based ona bad understanding of
transform. I'm still at a bit of a loss, but, with the help of a
loop, I think I have a way of doing this, if inelegantly. Any more
elegant solutions would be appreciated, but, for now, it works!

set.seed(2001)
library(plyr)
library(ggplot2)
a<-data.frame(g=as.factor(rep(c(1,2,3),2000)), b=rnorm(2000*3),

d=rnorm(2000*3))

maxscale<-function(x) x/max(x, na.rm=T)

#loop over variables
#creating two dummy variables, temp and nv, to be later renamed
for(avar in c("b", "d")){
a$temp<-a[[avar]]
a <- ddply(a, .(g), transform, nv=maxscale(temp))
a[[paste(avar, "1", sep="")]]<-a$nv #the renaming
}

#cleanup
a<-a[,-which(names(a)%in% c("nv", "temp"))]
#this should plot three lines
qplot(d, d1, facets=~g, data=a)

messages.subject: Re: ddply and generating matrix output of unequal size
parts:
Hi:

I think this particular case can be done a bit more simply with

> b <- ddply(a, .(g), transform, b1 = maxscale(b), d1 = maxscale(d))

but it's certainly a problem if you want to apply the function to, say,  ten or more numeric variables.

This 'works':

ddply(a, .(g),  numcolwise(maxscale))

This doesn't:
ddply(a, .(g),  transform, numcolwise(maxscale))

In the former case, the maxscale function is applied to both numeric columns and returns a data frame with the original variable names. I'm guessing that because of the transform argument in the latter call, the original column names would get overwritten, so it returns the original data frame by default and fails to append the transformed columns.

I tried using the colwise() approach and tried to write a function that changes the name of the output vector that could be used in numcolwise(), but unfortunately my attempts were in vain.
I could change the name of the rescaled variable with assign(), and it shows up in ls() of the function's local environment, but I couldn't figure out how to return it with that name. [I also tried rename() in the reshape package, but it didn't work on the output vector.]  FWIW, here's my lame attempt:

maxscale2 <- function(x) {
          ms <- x/max(x, na.rm=T)
          u <- paste(substitute(x), '1', sep = '')
          assign(u, ms)     # Good up to here...
###          return(???)  [at least five different attempts failed]
    }

If fed a vector named x, u will return 'x1', and assign will generate a new vector named x1 in the local environment, but I haven't figured out how to get the function to return x1 in such a way that ddply() will use x1 as its column name when called inside numcolwise(). Alas, computing on the language usually brings me to my knees :(

It would be nice to be able to assign names to the output columns of colwise() and friends inline, particularly in the context of transform, but I don't see an easy way to do that without partially rewriting the function.

Perhaps Hadley or one of the other list gurus can provide some feedback...

Dennis




The plot I got out of this seemed to be consistent with yours

On Fri, Feb 18, 2011 at 12:12 PM, jebyrnes <byr...@nceas.ucsb.edu> wrote:
Sorry, that was incorrect and based ona  bad understanding of
transform.  I'm still at a bit of a loss, but, with the help of a
loop, I think I have a way of doing this, if inelegantly.  Any more
elegant solutions would be appreciated, but, for now, it works!

set.seed(2001)
library(plyr)
library(ggplot2)
a<-data.frame(g=as.factor(rep(c(1,2,3),2000)), b=rnorm(2000*3),
d=rnorm(2000*3))

maxscale<-function(x) x/max(x, na.rm=T)

#loop over variables
#creating two dummy variables, temp and nv, to be later renamed
for(avar in c("b", "d")){
       a$temp<-a[[avar]]
       a <- ddply(a, .(g),  transform,  nv=maxscale(temp))
       a[[paste(avar, "1", sep="")]]<-a$nv #the renaming
}

#cleanup
a<-a[,-which(names(a)%in% c("nv", "temp"))]



#this should plot three lines
qplot(d, d1, facets=~g, data=a)
